title: Mining in Eastern Africa
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts (to confirm): tanzanite only in Tanzania (Mererani); gold and diamonds in Tanzania; soda ash at Lake Magadi; copper in Uganda (Kilembe). Mercury from small gold mines poisons water.

skills.key_step: The child names the minerals of Eastern Africa and where each is found.

floor.prerequisite: Names Kenya's minerals and where they are mined.
floor.question: Where is soda ash mined?

board.say: Which country is it mined in?

misconceptions.ask: Where is soda ash mined in Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which lake is salty and in the south of the Rift.
Say tanzanite takes its name from the country.
Ask: dug from the ground or grown?

misconceptions.ask: Is the oil found in Turkana a mineral resource?
misconceptions.repair: List minerals in all forms: solid (gold), liquid (oil).

checks.question: In which country is tanzanite mined?
Name a mineral mined in Kenya.
checks.answer: any of: soda ash, fluorspar, titanium, gold, limestone

skills.key_step: The child describes mining methods and how some minerals are taken out.

floor.question: Name a mineral mined in Uganda.

representations: a pan with sand and water
photos of a quarry and a shaft
steps: Name a mineral it is used for.
Say why that method suits it.

board.do: Draw a wide pit and a narrow shaft.

misconceptions.repair: Show a quarry at the coast.
Ask what a pan and water can do to find gold.

misconceptions.ask: How is soda ash taken from Lake Magadi?
misconceptions.repair: Show a photo of the white crust on Lake Magadi.
Compare a quarry photo with a tunnel drawing.

checks.question: Which method is used for limestone?
What is panning?
checks.answer: washing gravel in water to find gold

skills.key_step: The child explains the effects of mining on the environment and ways of repairing them.

floor.question: What is open-cast mining?
floor.answer: digging an open pit from the surface

board.do: Draw an open pit filled with water.

board.say: Why is this dangerous, and how is it repaired?

board.do: Wait for "people can drown; fill and plant".
Write two harms and two repairs.

misconceptions.ask: What does open-cast mining leave behind?
How can a mined area be repaired?
misconceptions.repair: Talk about Haller Park in Mombasa.

misconceptions.ask: How can small gold mines harm rivers?
misconceptions.repair: Show a picture of a warning sign at a polluted river.

listen_for: There are none; mining gives jobs
misconceptions.ask: Give one bad effect of mining.
misconceptions.repair: Use a T-chart with both sides.

checks.question: Give two harmful effects of mining.
checks.answer: any two of: holes, destroyed land and forest, dust and noise, poisoned water

checks.question: Give one way of repairing land after mining.
checks.answer: any of: refilling pits, replanting trees, treating waste
